title: The Monsoon of the Empty Quarter
premise: Odile Sandoval, estranged son of disgraced archaeologist Marisol Sandoval, inherits her debts and her brass compass, which points not north but toward whatever its last holder loved most. When a freak tide exposes a cave in the Empty Quarter's coastal range — the same cave Marisol vanished searching for — Odile joins the salvage expedition of the man who betrayed her mother, half to settle the debt, half to learn the truth. As the monsoon breaks early and the passes begin to close, Odile must choose between exposing the betrayal that destroyed his family and protecting the found family of diggers, guides, and thieves who have become his own. He crosses the range ahead of the snows, confronts the betrayer at the cave's sealed heart, and chooses truth over vengeance — publishing his mother's findings under her name and walking out with the compass finally pointing home.
about_author: Emrys Lockridge is the pen name of a former field surveyor who spent six years mapping coastlines from Oman to the Hebrides before turning to fiction. Known for adventure novels steeped in real terrain and quieter emotional weather, Lockridge writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Tide
chapters.summary: Odile Sandoval, POV. Working a salvage dock to pay his mother's creditors, Odile watches a spring tide peel back the seabed to reveal a cave mouth ringed with prehistoric carvings — the exact cave from Marisol's final letters. The emotional beat: dread disguised as opportunity, as the debt collector arrives the same hour with an expedition contract bearing a familiar name.

chapters.title: A Compass That Lies
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Sorting Marisol's effects, Odile tests the brass compass and finds its needle swings toward people, not north — toward him when he holds it, toward the sea when Marisol's letters are near. He signs the expedition contract despite learning the expedition chief is Cassian Vey, the protégé who testified against Marisol. Beat: resentment hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Crew of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Odile, POV, introducing ensemble. At the staging camp Odile meets the crew: Yusuf the guide with a forged license, Petra the explosives expert hiding a tremor, and sixteen-year-old Naji who stowed away to escape an arranged marriage. Each carries a secret debt. Beat: wary camaraderie forming among people who expect to be abandoned.

chapters.title: Vey's Version of the Truth
chapters.summary: Odile and Vey, alternating. Vey offers Odile a partnership and his own account of Marisol's disgrace: she falsified the cave's dating to secure funding, and Vey merely reported it. Odile's compass needle steadies on Vey — meaning Vey loved something truly, once. Beat: doubt seeded; the reader begins suspecting everyone, including the dead.

chapters.title: Into the Range
chapters.summary: Yusuf, POV. The expedition enters the coastal range as weather satellites show the monsoon forming weeks early. Yusuf navigates by childhood memory of goat paths now washed away, and privately recognizes the cave carvings from stories his grandmother called forbidden. Beat: the land itself begins resisting them; wonder braided with warning.

chapters.title: What the Cave Charged Admission For
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. First descent into the tide cave: a drowned antechamber of star charts and a stone door that only opens when the compass is held against it — proof Marisol had been here. Inside, Odile finds her field journal, half waterlogged, contradicting Vey's account. Beat: grief and vindication arriving together, too tangled to feel.

chapters.title: The Journal's Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Odile and Petra, alternating. The journal's final pages are torn out, and the only knife marks match a blade Petra recognizes — she once sold such blades to Vey's expeditions. Petra says nothing. Meanwhile Naji is caught reading over Odile's shoulder, and instead of angering him, becomes his confidant. Beat: complicity spreading; secrets multiplying faster than trust.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Yusuf, POV. A shepherd's village warns the passes will close in nine days, not the month the expedition planned for. Vey refuses to turn back, citing the funding deadline that ruined Marisol. Odile realizes Vey is reenacting her mother's fatal schedule. Beat: the first open fracture in the expedition's unity.

chapters.title: Ninety Meters of Bad Rock
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. A rockfall traps Naji and Odile in a side gallery; Petra must place charges with her tremoring hands while Yusuf anchors the line. The rescue succeeds but consumes two days of their window. Beat: the crew stops being a payroll and becomes a family — precisely when the deadline makes that dangerous.

chapters.title: The Compass Points at Naji
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Recovering, Naji touches the compass and the needle locks onto him. Odile realizes Marisol's compass points to whatever its holder loves most — and that Marisol's last fix must have been the cave itself, or someone in it. Beat: the mystery pivots from what happened to whom Marisol loved, and why that destroyed her.

chapters.title: Vey's Confession, Partial
chapters.summary: Vey, POV, first time fully inside his head. Vey admits he tore the pages: Marisol's journal proved the cave was genuine and her dating honest, and his testimony was bought by the funder who wanted her discredited and the site private. But he claims he did it to protect Odile from her debts — a self-serving half-truth. Beat: sympathy and fury in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Split at Cold Fork
chapters.summary: Ensemble, rotating brief POVs. At the high pass fork, Vey orders the team onward while Yusuf declares the weather makes it suicidal. The crew splits: Yusuf, Naji, and Petra will cache supplies and hold the descent route; Odile goes with Vey to the cave's inner door. Beat: loyalty tested structurally — the family divides so someone can survive.

chapters.title: The Inner Door
chapters.summary: Odile and Vey, alternating. At the sealed heart of the cave, the compass opens the door to a chamber Marisol reached alive: intact murals proving her chronology, and evidence someone else was there after her — recent boot prints, modern resin, a removed artifact. Beat: the revelation that Marisol may not have died of exposure alone.

chapters.title: What Marisol Found
chapters.summary: Odile, POV, reading recovered pages. Marisol's restored journal reveals she discovered the funder's plan to strip the site and sell it abroad, and that she stayed to document everything — and that Vey's testimony, however bought, gave her cover to hide the evidence where only the compass could find it. Beat: the mother's final act reframed as a message to her child.

chapters.title: The Storm Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Yusuf, POV. The monsoon hits the range a full day ahead of forecast; the cache route floods, stranding the descent party. Yusuf must reroute through his grandmother's forbidden path — the one the carvings mark. Beat: the land's warnings fulfilled; the forbidden path as both salvation and reckoning.

chapters.title: Petra's Tremor
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. On the forbidden path, Petra's condition worsens; she confesses she sold Vey the blade and has been reporting the expedition's progress to the funder to clear her own debts. The crew's fury is interrupted by a rockslide — Petra spends her last charges saving them. Beat: betrayal and sacrifice in one body; forgiveness deferred, not denied.

chapters.title: The Funder's Men
chapters.summary: Odile and Vey, alternating. Descending from the inner chamber, Odile and Vey are ambushed by the funder's salvage team, who have tracked them via Petra's reports — and who intend to take the chamber's contents and leave no witnesses. Vey, for the first time, chooses Marisol's side. Beat: the betrayer's redemption purchased at gunpoint.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. A running descent through flooding galleries, the compass guiding them where the murals show the ancient escape route — the cave's builders faced this same storm. Naji's voice finds them through the flooded passage on the far side. Beat: the cave itself as ancestor and ally; terror giving way to awe.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Flood
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The parties reunite at the forbidden path's mouth as the range disappears behind rain. Vey confesses everything to the crew, offering himself to the funder's men as a distraction. Yusuf refuses the sacrifice — no one is left behind on this mountain. Beat: found family made explicit and costly.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the Pass
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Cornered at the pass, Odile negotiates with the funder's lead man using the one thing they cannot dig up elsewhere: Marisol's complete documentation, which he'll surrender only if the site is protected and his mother's name restored. The compass needle, held by the funder's man, spins wildly — he loves nothing. Beat: truth as the only currency that holds value.

chapters.title: Snow on the Empty Quarter
chapters.summary: Vey, POV. The first snow falls as they cross the final col. Vey, wounded from the ambush, gives Odile his testimony in writing — full, unguarded, damning himself — and asks only that Marisol's name lead the publication. Beat: the betrayer's last gift; grief finally allowed its own shape.

chapters.title: Where the Needle Rests
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Months later: Marisol's findings published under her name, the cave declared protected, Vey serving his sentence and reading Odile's letters. On the dock where the story began, Odile holds the compass and watches the needle settle — pointing not at the sea, not at the cave, but at Naji, Yusuf, and Petra waiting with tea. Beat: home redefined as the people the needle loves; loyalty and truth reconciled at last.
